original.prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the Public Examinations Act amendment bill introduced in July 2026:
items: Maximum fine for individual offenders — INR 50 lakh
Maximum fine for organised offences — INR 5 crore
Deadline for completing investigations — two months
original.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
original.explain: Organised offences would carry fines of up to INR 10 crore and at least seven years in prison. INR 5 crore is the maximum fine for complicit service providers. The individual fine ceiling rises fivefold to INR 50 lakh, and investigations must finish within two months.
original.source: Organised offences would carry at least seven years and fines of up to INR 10 crore (~ USD 1 million).

rewritten.prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the Public Examinations Act amendment bill introduced in July 2026:
items: Maximum fine for individual offenders — INR 50 lakh
Maximum fine for organised offences — INR 5 crore
Deadline for completing investigations — three months
rewritten.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
rewritten.explain: Only pair 1 is correct, as the individual fine ceiling rises fivefold to INR 50 lakh. Pair 2 is wrong because organised offences carry fines of up to INR 10 crore (INR 5 crore applies to complicit service providers), and pair 3 is wrong because investigations must finish within two months. Three months is the deadline from charge sheet to verdict in Special Fast Track Courts.
rewritten.source: Investigations would have to finish within two months, with Courts of Session designated as Special Fast Track Courts running day-to-day trials and a three-month deadline from charge sheet to verdict.
